To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

p8K and p6K are localized in different subcellular compartments, p8K being associated with the cytoplasmic fibrous structures and p6K with plasmodesmatal regions, and the two proteins accumulate at different stages during the course of the infection.

the movement protein p8K of olive latent virus accumulates in the fibrous inclusions of infected cells and is not detected in the soluble fraction, while its counterpart p6K is not detected in fibrous inclusion bodies but is detected in the soluble protein fraction of infected cells.
the two movement proteins of olive virus 1 (p6K and p8K) have distinct localization in infected tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunological characterization of the two viral proteins p8K and p6K, and their subcellular location in infected tissues.
the subcellular localization and intracellular immunodetection of p8K and p6K, two of the movement proteins of olive latently infected virus 1, in infected Nicotianabenthamiana plants.
the localization of the movement proteins of OLV1 and the characterization of the fibrous structures observed in infected cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the movement protein p8K of OLV1 accumulates in the fibrous structures, whereas p6K accumulates in plasmodesmatal membranes.
p8K and p6K, as other movement proteins, accumulate in the cytoplolumn and in plasmodesmatal areas of the cells.

the two movement proteins of olive laten virus 1 are present in the cytosol, the fibrous inclusions and, in the case of p6K, near plasmodesma, but the specific serum to p8K did not recognize its antigen in the cytoplamic fibrils of the infected cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

p8K is the main movement protein of OLVi, being the one involved in the formation of the fibrous inclusions and, therefore, likely the protein that mediates cell-to-cell movement. p6K is a minor movement protein that is also involved in the cell-to-cell movement of OLVi, but it does not participate in the formation of fibrous inclusions.

the two movement proteins are localized in different cell compartments. p8K is present in membranous structures and/or cell organells and, in addition, is the major protein component in the cytoplamic fibrous structures. p6K seems to be associated to plasmodesmatal channels.
the movement protein encoded by ORF4 of OLV-1 (p6K), is not involved in the formation of the fibrous structures in the cytoplASM of locally and systemical infected cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p8K, but not p6K, is a constituent of the fibrous inclusions present in cells infected with olive latent virus
the movement protein encoded by ORF3 (p8k) accumulates in the cytoplamic fibrous inclusions, which are the sites of virus replication and cell-to-cell movement.
the two movement proteins of olive latently infected tissues are localized to different subcellular compartments, and that the p8K protein is associated with the cytoplasmic fibrous structures.
